universalAnswers.whatHappened: OpenAI announced a US advertiser test of Sponsored Agents.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: An optional seller-sponsored conversation opened after a person clicks a ChatGPT ad.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: No independent usage, effectiveness, privacy, data-sharing, global or tier-availability evidence.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A shopper should recognize the move from an original chat into a seller’s sales conversation.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: People who see a participating advertiser’s ChatGPT ad and choose the sponsored conversation.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Select US advertisers are testing the format; broader availability is not stated.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: The source does not establish how often people will see or use it, or how useful it will be.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Notice the label and compare product claims with the seller’s product page.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Who is speaking in this chat, and what do they want me to do?

model-tool-release.productRange: Sponsored Agents are an optional business-sponsored conversation after a person clicks a ChatGPT ad.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: A person can choose to ask follow-up product or service questions in a clearly labelled, separate seller conversation.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: Low-stakes questions about a product or service offered by the advertiser.
model-tool-release.notFor: The source does not establish neutral shopping advice, effectiveness, privacy practice, data-sharing practice or broader availability.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: The source distinguishes the sponsored conversation from the person’s original chat and ChatGPT’s independent answers.
model-tool-release.availability: OpenAI says it is testing Sponsored Agents with select advertisers in the United States; it gives no broader availability details.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: The announcement does not state a user free-or-paid boundary for this test.
model-tool-release.costBoundary: The announcement does not state a user price or purchase requirement for starting the conversation.
model-tool-release.limitations: Provider announcement only; no independent usage or outcome evidence.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: The article gives one original lamp-shopping example and no technical implementation claim.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: OpenAI is the source for the existence and described design of its own test; every product claim remains attributed or source-bounded.

translation.newsVersionExact: OpenAI announced September 16 that it is testing Sponsored Agents with select US advertisers.
translation.actualMeaningExact: You are talking to a seller about what it offers, through an AI agent inside ChatGPT.
translation.mechanismExact: After clicking an ad in ChatGPT, a person can choose to open a clearly labelled conversation with an agent sponsored by that business.
translation.familiarExampleExact: Imagine an ad for a desk lamp catches your eye.

jargon.plainMeaning: “Sponsored” tells you who is paying for the conversation.

learningConnections.concept: Commercial incentives shape what a speaker wants you to do
learningConnections.learningPayoff: Ask who is speaking and what incentive sits behind a claim.
